name_reason: Compliant with fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention (domain=enemy data table accessor). No address residue. Accurately reflects the function's purpose: returns a pointer into the read-only enemy stat table. All 4 callers use it exactly as a per-enemy data-entry accessor.
purpose: Leaf .object3 table accessor: returns a pointer to the idx-th 10-byte entry of the read-only enemy stat table (data_fd2_battle_enemy_data_table @ 0x61AF9).
logic_summary: Pure address arithmetic, no side effects. Returns base 0x61AF9 + idx*0xA, i.e. &data_fd2_battle_enemy_data_table[idx]. Standard EBP-based frame; MUL EDX with EDX=0xA (10-byte stride), ADD base. The returned pointer is the entry start (offset 0 = bRA). Callers index into it with field offsets (+2 HP word, +4 MP, +5 AP, +6 DP, +7 DX, +8 MV/magic_resist, +9 EX).

params.name: idx
params.semantics: Enemy-relative index into the 68-entry enemy_data table = (runtime char portrait/class id - 0x44), range 0..0x43. All callers compute it as bPortrait_id/bChar_id - 0x44 before calling.
params.reason: Matches the live Ghidra and src signature name; 'idx' is an acceptable generic-index name for a pure table accessor and has no address residue. Body and source both use 'idx'.

returns.semantics: Pointer to the start of the idx-th 10-byte enemy_data entry (= &data_fd2_battle_enemy_data_table[idx]; offset 0 is the bRA field). Caller dereferences fields by offset.

comment_original_issue: src comment was correct but terse: it did not state the index convention (idx = id - 0x44) nor the entry field layout, which is load-bearing context for readers. Augmented with both (verified against fd2-knowledge enemy_entry: RA CL HP HP MP AP DP DX MV EX, and against all 4 callers). Ghidra plate was outdated: claimed 'remaining 1 byte per entry not fully mapped (likely padding)' but all 10 bytes are mapped, and it listed HP as a single named byte when +2 is a uint16.
notes: Cross-verified against fd2-knowledge skill (enemy_entry struct = 10 bytes: RA CL HP HP MP AP DP DX MV EX, FD2.LE @ 0x558F9 sample / actual table @ 0x61AF9 in this build). All 4 callers confirmed: fd2_init_runtime_char_for_battle reads +0/+1 (class category), word +2 (HP*level), +4 (MP*level), +5 (AP*level), +6 (DP*level), +7 (DX*level), +8 (magic_resist); the other 3 read +9 (EX). Global symbol declared in globals.h:532 as 'const enemy_data data_fd2_battle_enemy_data_table[68]'; table data defined in btltab3.c:673. Note: byte +8 is labeled MV in the strategy guide but used as bMagic_resist for enemy spawns (player-class branch uses base[7] for the same runtime field) -- semantic nuance, not a defect. No logic changed; only src comment augmented and Ghidra plate corrected.
